To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Pareto tradeoff frontier for the multiobjective optimization of cutting parameters in the turning of J-Steel material can be identified by using the Efficient Global Optimization algorithm with a 36% reduction of the experimental samples compared to a full-factorial experimental design.

the Pareto frontier for the cutting parameters of turning operation for J-Steel material is a “knee-shaped” curve and the m-EGO optimization algorithm can be used to reduce the number of experimental samples required to identify the frontier.
“The cutting parameters for J-Steel material can be optimized to achieve reasonable compromise between good surface quality (Ra, Rz, and Rmax), and high material removal rates (MRR).”
In summary, our research is concerned with
a multiobjective approach for identifying the Pareto frontier for cutting parameters in turning operations for a difficult-to-cut material.
the optimization of cutting parameters in a turning operation for a J-Steel material.
identifying the Pareto frontier of the cutting parameters for the machining of J-Steel material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pareto frontier is a “knee-shaped” surface, which has a good range in which both objectives are good, while the other range has one of the two objectives being poor.
the Pareto frontier for the multiobjective turning optimization problem for J-Steel material is a convex function of the cutting parameters.
the cutting parameters should be set at the following values: 0.1 mm/rev for feed rate, 150 m/min for cutting speed, and 0.5 mm for depth of cut.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a proper selection for the cutting parameters in turning operations can lead to a good compromise between high material removal rate and good surface quality for a heat-treated J-Steel material.

the m-EGO is a promising alternative to the full-factorial experimental design for identifying the Pareto frontier of the multiobjective optimization problem, but the trade-off frontier should be identified first via the full-factorial approach.
the multiobjective optimization approach can be successfully applied to identify a good trade-off frontier for turning operation of a heat-treated alloy J-Steel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the m-EGO approach can provide an effective alternative for identifying trade-off frontier for multiobjective optimization of cutting parameters in machining.

the m-EGO can be a powerful tool in the design and optimization of cutting processes, especially in cases where the trade-off frontier is not known a priori and where the number of experimental samples is limited.

the Pareto frontier of cutting parameters for the turning operation of J-Steel material is a “knee”, in which certain cutting parameters settings are able to achieve a good compromise between surface quality and material removal rate.
